Pandemic is Triggering Me

TW: Rape

After another sleepless night, I have to finally get this out. This is the only safe place I know where to put it without being further shamed. 

Over a decade ago, I was raped. After many years of counseling, I thought I'd dealt with all my triggers: certain smells, touches, and similar voices. I worked really hard in therapy and I'm so proud of how far I've come. I have a healthy marriage with a very supportive husband. 

I put it behind me and I rarely got flashbacks anymore... Until the pandemic. One trigger I never thought I'd have to deal with is having a cloth put over my face. I honestly didn't even realize it was a trigger, but over the past 13 years, I've never been able to wear a turtle neck or wear a full face mask at Halloween. No big deal until mask mandates came out. 

I want it to be clear that I fully support mask wearing and after 6 more months of intense counseling I'm now able to wear a mask, with a plastic cage insert between the cloth and my face. 

What I didn't expect is how everyday, other people would force me to relive my trauma. When the mask mandate came out, I immediately went to my Dr and my counselor. They both wrote medical notes for me to wear a face shield. My dr helped me pick out an appropriate full face shield and I wore it everytime I left the house, always sanitizing it before and after use. They put the reason on the medical note as "anxiety"  to prevent outing me as a SA survivor. My work wouldn't accept this, I had to go through 2 months of teleworking (not easy in my job) filling out paperwork and constantly having to re-explain to several officials about my SA. That's when the nightmares started coming back. I fully understand wanting to protect my coworkers but all of them were ok with it and didn't understand why I couldn't just wear a shield. I worked in a small office with an office away from everyone else and a door that closes. If that was it, then I think I could have dealt with it. 

Grocery shopping was a nightmare. I would regularly get customers shaming me verbally despite always first calling the store to explain my situation and the manager always approving my in person visit to their store with a face shield. Other people would be in the store with no face covering at all but either I didn't hear comments made to them, or I seemed to be an easier target. I started doing grocery delivery and stopped going anywhere but work and home. 

Then the medical field made me fully relive the trauma. I was under a lot of stress and started having chest pains. After 5 hours of it not subsiding, I called my Dr and they immediately made an appointment for me to come in. My husband was away so I had to drive myself. As soon as I arrived, the nurse started shoving a mask in my face and getting really pushy about me wearing it. I tried to hand her the note that the physician of that office wrote me and she refused it. Along with chest pains, I'm now having a full blown

Went today and there was no change from last weeks empty sac. It’s actually even smaller. My doctor looked really sad and I think he only actually called it what it is after he saw I had accepted it already. It’s kind of like a weird sense of closure if I’m being honest. 

Now I go back in a week and hopefully I pass it by then? I had brown spotting before but it stopped 😐

​On Loss Remembrance Day, I'm sharing the nightmare of my missed miscarriage—and how the subsequent medical system trauma was a brutal blow after years of chronic health struggles (TW)

It feels fitting to post my recent miscarriage loss on International Pregnancy and Infant Loss Remembrance Day. Please be kind with me and this long post. It feels like the only thing giving me any peace right now. 


My husband and I have been married for more than 9 years, together almost 13. I have struggled with an autoimmune condition (ulcerative colitis) since I was 19 (I'm almost 35 now) so we have put off starting a family until my chronic health issues were in better shape. 2025 felt like the right time and when we found out I was pregnant, it felt like maybe the universe was sending us a sign that after all my years of health struggles, maybe pregnancy wouldn’t be the same uphill climb. 

We were devastated after we couldn't find a heartbeat at our 9+4 ultrasound, especially since everything had looked normal at our 7-week scan. When we found out that our baby had died at 7+3 and I didn't know for more than two weeks, I felt so let down by my body, which I already had complicated feelings about due to the autoimmune issues. This was all bad enough, but navigating healthcare support in Ontario after the miscarriage was another painful blow and a clear indication to me that women who miscarry don't matter. My family doctor took days to get back to me to confirm the pregnancy loss, left me to arrange my own evacuation and ignored an abnormal cyst that showed up on my ultrasound, indicating I might have endometriosis. I was sent on a pointless hospital miscarriage consult that resulted in further delays in scheduling a D&C. As a result, I had a traumatic, unplanned miscarriage at home, flushing my baby down the toilet and passing out twice due to blood loss and a history of anemia. I ended up being taken by ambulance to a nearby ER and after 12 hours there, nearly passing out a third time, multiple IVs, a painful pelvic exam with no pain meds, I had an emergency D&C (thankfully under general anesthesia). 

After this experience, I had my family doctor question my need for short-term medical leave from work and at a scheduled appointment with my OBGYN in a waiting room full of pregnant women just last week, I had to relive this whole traumatic experience over again because she and her staff didn't know I had miscarried. 


I am left shocked and traumatized by my loss, but also by the systemic neglect and lack of compassion I was shown during the most vulnerable time of my life. It’s no surprise that my ulcerative colitis has since flared and I feel emotionally exhausted. None of this is helped by the fact that several close friends and family have recently had their babies or are nearly full-term pregnant. It all hurts deeply.

Pregnant with an IUD in Texas, resources and how I got an abortion.

Hi, I posted my story in TwoXChromosomes and was hoping to share what I learned here. I had never been pregnant or had an abortion, and didn't know how to do any of this either. 

My situation: I got pregnant with a copper IUD, Paragard, in Texas. It was not ectopic, but the IUD embedded and the doctor could not legally help me as I was just after 6 weeks. Because the IUD was still in, I could not have a medical abortion. I had to schedule an appointment for a surgical abortion out-of-state, arrange travel and lodging, and contact abortion funds for financial help. I waited most of the day for my appointment, but my surgical procedure went very smoothly - the doctors and clinic staff were empathetic, kind, and took good care of me. Apart from some expected bleeding and cramping, my physical recovery was quick.

Google searches, Reddit, and healthcare websites have so many helpful resources, but it's all in different places left for you to figure out what to do in what order. So, here's my checklist/action list if you need an abortion.

➕➕➕➕➕

**For the next shocked and scared woman who needs help and needs and abortion.**

➕ If you have both an IUD and positive pregnancy test, schedule an appointment with an OBYGYN to make sure it's not ectopic. You will need to have blood samples taken probably two days apart. They will test for HCG levels (pregnancy hormone) - in a normal pregnancy, the levels should double every two days; in an ectopic pregnancy, the levels will not. The doctor should also schedule an ultrasound, which will definitely show if the pregnancy is ectopic or not.

They'll probably try removing the IUD regardless of your choice to continue or terminate. Removal has a chance of miscarriage.

➕ Regardless of if you have an IUD - schedule an ultrasound, which will determine how far along you are. Expect abdominal and/or vaginal ultrasounds. Don't bother with Clearblue tests which will give you a vague week estimate, and if you go to Planned Parenthood make sure it's an ultrasound, not just a urine sample that will tell you yes/no there's HCG.

If you're in Texas, don't be scared of the new law. It targets people who help others with abortions (doctors/providers), the actual recipient of an abortion. You can still terminate, but beyond 6 weeks they can't directly help you with any procedure.

➕ Make your choice. Whatever you decide, it's okay. It is the right decision for you. You are still a beautiful, strong, capable, worthy human, and you can do this.

➕ If you choose to terminate: medical abortion (pill) at home

[Aid Access](https://aidaccess.org/) will give you a prescription and directions for mifepristone and misoprostol for $150, or however much you can afford. Miscarriage with very little bleeding

I'm wondering if anybody else has experienced miscarriage with very little bleeding or if it this means that it is likely that my miscarriage still isn't complete (of course, I am seeking help from medical professionals, but I am hoping to find out if anybody else went through a similar timeline). Here's my timeline: 

\- minor spotting appeared at 5w6d (no flow, clots or cramping), I called my OB practice as a precaution, they scheduled an ultrasound for 6w1d - this ultrasound showed gestational sac measuring 5w1d, but no other signs 

\-OB told me it may be a dating issue or an embryo that stopped developing, ordered two bHCG tests roughly 48h apart (late Fri afternoon, early Mon morning) and repeat ultrasound on 6w5d to confirm which one is it. 

\- 6w3d - I started bleeding, it was a fairly light flow, but clots and cramping were present. The bleeding never escalated from there, and cramping was on-off. 

\- 6w4d bHCG shows a small rise from 1200 to 1500 in over 48h, so it's clear to me that this pregnancy is not progressing the way it should. 

\-6w5d - ultrasound shows the gest.sac still measuring 5w1d, no sign of fetal pole or heartbeat, miscarriage not diagnosed but indicated. Based on the advice of my OB, I decided to take mifeprex+miso to end the pregnancy as I could not bear the thought of expectant management and OB strongly discouraged D&C. I took mifeprex at the office, and miso the next day (25h after mifeprex)

\-6w6d - about 2h after taking miso, I started having really intense cramping (worse than the worst period pain I have experienced ever) and expected the bleeding to begin, but it never really happened. There would be some blood on the toilet tissue, but no active flow nor have I filled a single pad. I could have gone through the entire process with daily panty liners. 

7w - OB advised me to go to an ER because of lack of bleeding to make sure I was not experiencing ectopic pregnancy. bHCG dropped from 1500 to 500, while ultrasound showed that gestational sac is still there.
